Scalar round adds original input into adjacent lane and low32*high32 keyed product into current lane. AArch64 helper uses umaddl for32-bit widening multiply-add. Scramble xors shift47/secret then multiplies by prime modulo64.

NEON and scalar complete eight-lane accumulator arrays match after accumulation and scramble for65536 total controls, including deliberately unaligned input/secret offsets. This is backend parity, not independent fullhash oracle.

VSX handles byte order via reviewed helpers; SVE adapts lane count with masked2/4/8-element loads and keeps accumulator across stripes. LSX uses128-bit widening products. Those backends not executed on ARM NEON host.

Backend bindings select scalar secret initializer for NEON/VSX/SVE/LSX. Size optimization>=1 forces scalar secret initialization even for other backends. Common long-key loop prefix uses secret-derived stripes per block; body remains unread.
